title.narrative: Co-designing integrated water solutions in Bangkok – Putting the Water as Leverage Principles in practice

description.narrative: This assignment formed part of the Water as Leverage (WaL) programme and aimed to strengthen collaboration between the Netherlands and Thailand, particularly with the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA). Through design-driven research, workshops, and outreach activities, the programme demonstrated the added value of integrated and inclusive approaches to urban water management. Organised in close collaboration with the Netherlands embassy in Bangkok, Thailand, RVO, Deltares, and other partners, the initiative applied the WaL Guidance and Principles in the Bangkok context to enhance visibility and foster community-centered urban water regeneration across Southeast Asia. Workshop reports and an executive summary of the WaL Academy Bangkok trajectory – describing the first three years of this initiative – can be downloaded on this page.The Netherlands embassy in Bangkok, Thailand, together with the Office of the National Water Resources (ONWR), the Royal Irrigation Department (RID), and the BMA, hosted a multi-stakeholder design workshop under the Water as Leverage programme. Supported by national and international partners, the initiative sought to foster climate-resilient water management in Bangkok through systemic co-design processes and Nature-Based Solutions (NbS).The two-day Water as Leverage Academy Bangkok workshop brought together Thai and international experts, including engineers, academics, civil society representatives, the private sector, and government officials. Participants explored the challenges facing Bangkok's canal systems – such as flooding, pollution, and the loss of cultural connection – through interactive mapping, field analysis, and collaborative design exercises. Key tools included the Three Water City Game and a Serious Game on systemic problem-solving, which encouraged systems thinking and collaboration across sectors.Proposals developed during the workshop highlighted hybrid and inclusive approaches that integrated NbS with Thai cultural heritage. Concepts included electric boat corridors, green canal edges, tourism-linked cultural zones, and community-led governance mechanisms. Collectively, these ideas reimagined Bangkok’s canals as multifunctional assets – serving as flood buffers, cultural corridors, and green mobility networks – rather than solely as drainage systems.
